title: Money does not burn — it moves rooms
hook: Headlines say a trillion dollars was wiped out. Where did it actually go?
metaphor: Picture a house with four rooms: stocks, bonds, gold, and cash. People walk between rooms. The house never loses anybody.
body: When stocks fall hard, that money usually shows up somewhere else.
Often it moves into bonds or gold, which feel safer.
So a crash in one place is often a flood into another.
Watching which room fills up tells you what people are afraid of.

live.template: Today money is mostly moving toward {flow_to}. The map shows {edge_count} main paths.

caveat: Some value really does vanish when prices fall. The rotation idea explains direction, not every dollar.
